title: RFL Skill ISA composition file
description: Validates a Skill ISA composition file (the JSON / YAML form an author writes; reference instance examples/01-cable-insertion/skill.yaml). Structural validation per 01-skill-isa.md: the compositional algebra (sequence / parallel / reactive / repeat / branch / let-bind), that every primitive call key is one of the 50 ISA primitive ids, and that an extension call is namespaced ext.<ns>.<name>. Per-primitive parameter names, types, units, and enums are constrained only for primitives precisely typed so far (approach B, tightened one primitive at a time — currently grasp.pinch § 2.1, sense.locate § 7.4, transport.move_to_pose § 4.1, reach.align § 1.3, grasp.release § 2.10, reach.to_pose § 1.1, reach.approach § 1.2, reach.hover § 1.5, reach.scan § 1.6); every other primitive's params is an open object. Backs conformance test class 1 (parser conformance, 05-conformance.md). The algebra is the abstract BNF of 01 § Compositional algebra; this schema fixes its concrete YAML serialization, where a let-bind is a sequence statement {let, from} whose binding scopes over the rest of the enclosing sequence (the BNF's explicit in(...) is accepted as an optional key).

description.description: Human-readable summary of what the skill does.

body.description: The skill body: a single Composition (typically a sequence).

ObjectMap.description: Task object references, keyed by local name. Each entry names an ObjectRef whose pose is resolved at runtime by a sense.* primitive (01 § Object reference).

ref.description: The object identity (ObjectRef) this local name binds to.

PrimitiveId.description: The 50 Skill ISA primitive ids, category.primitive in lowercase snake_case (01 § Provisional primitive enumeration). The enumeration is closed; extension primitives use the ext.<ns>.<name> form instead.

Params.description: A primitive's parameter block. Structurally an open object (or absent / null for a param-less call). This is the open floor that applies to every primitive; for primitives precisely typed so far it is intersected with a per-primitive schema via the allOf clauses of PrimitiveCall, so the precise schema is what binds for those keys.

Ref.description: A reference to a let-bound value (BNF Reference / Identifier): a bare identifier, optionally &-prefixed, naming a value bound earlier by a let-bind. In the serialized form any typed parameter may instead be such a reference (e.g. target: connector_t). The BNF's reserved terminals (auto, active, until, all, until_satisfied) are excluded so they are accepted only where a parameter's own schema lists them (Auto / GraspHandle / HoldDuration / Axes / Count); this keeps e.g. hold_duration: auto from sneaking in as a reference.

Axis.description: An unsigned principal axis of a frame (01 § Geometric types): x, y, or z. Distinct from SignedAxis (a +/- axis).

Auto.description: Defer the value to the Translation Layer's planner (BNF Auto). Accepted only where the spec types a parameter as T | auto.

Force.description: A force value (01 § Dimensioned scalars; canonical wire unit N): a unit-suffixed quantity string (N / kN / mN) or a let-reference.

Duration.description: A duration value (01 § Dimensioned scalars; canonical wire unit s): a unit-suffixed quantity string (s / ms), a let-reference, or auto.

Length.description: A length value (01 § Dimensioned scalars; canonical wire unit m, parameter tables may author in mm): a unit-suffixed quantity string (m / mm / cm) or a let-reference.

Ratio.description: A dimensionless ratio (01 § Dimensioned scalars), [0,1) unless stated: a number in that range or a let-reference.

HoldDuration.description: A hold duration (01 § reach.hover / force.push): a duration quantity (s / ms), the literal until (defer to an enclosing reactive), or a let-reference. Unlike Duration this does NOT accept auto.

Angle.description: An angle value (01 § Dimensioned scalars; canonical wire unit rad, parameter tables may author in deg): a unit-suffixed quantity string (deg / rad) or a let-reference.

Velocity.description: A linear-velocity value (01 § Dimensioned scalars; canonical wire unit m/s): a unit-suffixed quantity string (m/s) or a let-reference.

Acceleration.description: A linear-acceleration value (01 § Dimensioned scalars; canonical wire unit m/s^2): a unit-suffixed quantity string (m/s^2 or m/s²) or a let-reference.

AngularVelocity.description: An angular-velocity value (01 § Dimensioned scalars; canonical wire unit rad/s): a unit-suffixed quantity string (rad/s) or a let-reference.

FrameRef.description: A reference to a calibrated frame on the kinematic tree or in the world (01 § Geometric types). A frame name (e.g. task, receptacle, tcp_thumb).

SignedAxis.description: A signed principal axis of a frame (01 § Geometric types), e.g. -z. Symbolic tool-axis spellings (e.g. -tool_axis) are NOT this type and are not yet covered.

GraspHandle.description: A handle to an established grasp (01 § GraspRef): the literal active (the current grasp on the controlled frame) or a let-reference to a grasp bound earlier.

ContactResponse.description: Reaction to unplanned contact, shared across reach / transport primitives.

Axes.description: A set of principal axes, or all (01 § reach.align). Either the literal all or a non-empty array drawn from {x, y, z}.

GraspPinchParams.description: Parameters of grasp.pinch (01 § 2.1), precisely typed (approach B) — the eight parameters of the § 2.1 table, no more. target + force_budget are required; the rest carry the spec defaults. Any value may be a let-reference; auto is accepted only where the spec types the parameter as T | auto. The internal field typing of ObjectTarget / Pose6D / TactileTarget is a deeper increment — here each is an inline object or a reference.

target.description: ObjectTarget to pinch-grasp (perception-derived; typically reaches the call as a let-reference). An inline object or a let-reference.

force_budget.description: Max grip force, > 0; clamped to embodiment.limits.grip_force_max and target.max_contact_force if declared.

grasp_pose.description: Pose6D | auto — pinch contact-frame pose; auto = planner-derived from target geometry.

grasp_width.description: Length | auto — pre-close opening; auto = from target geometry.

tactile_target.description: TactileTarget | auto — contact-confirmation criterion in TactileManifold terms; auto = normal_force >= epsilon at >= 2 antipodal sites.

SenseLocateParams.description: Parameters of sense.locate (01 § 7.4), precisely typed (approach B). target_ref is required; the rest carry the spec defaults. auto is accepted only where the spec types the parameter as T | auto; Region internals are deferred (inline object or reference).

target_ref.description: ObjectRef | FeatureRef — the object identity / feature whose pose is estimated.

modality.description: Sensing modality (default auto = best available for the required precision).

required_precision.description: Length | auto — pose precision the result must achieve (default embodiment default).

search_region.description: Region | auto — where to look (default the expected vicinity).

frame.description: FrameRef — reference frame for the returned pose (default task).

TransportMoveToPoseParams.description: Parameters of transport.move_to_pose (01 § 4.1), precisely typed (approach B). target_pose is required; the rest carry the spec defaults. Pose6D internals are a deeper increment — here target_pose is an inline object or a reference.

grasp_handle.description: GraspRef | active (default active) — the grasp whose held object is transported.

target_pose.description: Pose6D — pose of the held object (not the effector) in frame. Inline object or let-reference.

max_acceleration.description: Acceleration | auto — clamped to the grasp's dynamic-stability limit.

clearance.description: Length >= 0 (default 0) — margin for the swept volume of object + effector.

contact_response.description: Reaction to unplanned contact of object or effector (default abort).

ReachAlignParams.description: Parameters of reach.align (01 § 1.3), precisely typed (approach B). target_frame is required; the rest carry the spec defaults.

axes.description: set<{x,y,z}> | all (default all) — controlled-frame axes to bring parallel to target_frame.

hold_position.description: Keep controlled_frame position fixed during rotation (default true).

position_tolerance.description: Length > 0 — drift bound while rotating (default 2 mm).

clearance.description: Length >= 0 (default 0) — margin to the static model over the swept volume.

GraspReleaseParams.description: Parameters of grasp.release (01 § 2.10), precisely typed (approach B). All parameters are optional (grasp_handle defaults to active), so a param-less call (null / empty) is valid.

grasp_handle.description: GraspRef | active (default active) — the grasp to release.

withdraw_axis.description: SignedAxis — direction to withdraw after opening (default -embodiment.default_tool_axis).

clearance_distance.description: Length | auto — distance to withdraw clear of the object envelope.

allow_drop.description: Permit release when the object is not stably supported (default false).

confirm_release.description: Verify no residual contact after opening (default true).

ReachToPoseParams.description: Parameters of reach.to_pose (01 § 1.1), precisely typed (approach B) — the nine parameters of the § 1.1 table, no more. target_pose is required; the rest carry the spec defaults. There is no acceleration parameter (unlike transport.move_to_pose). Pose6D internals are deferred (inline object or reference).

target_pose.description: Pose6D — goal pose of the controlled frame in frame; must admit >= 1 IK solution. Inline object or let-reference.

controlled_frame.description: FrameRef — a declared control frame (default embodiment.default_control_frame).

clearance.description: Length >= 0 (default 0) — minimum margin to the static collision model.

ReachApproachParams.description: Parameters of reach.approach (01 § 1.2), precisely typed (approach B) — the ten parameters of the § 1.2 table, no more. target + standoff are required; the rest carry the spec defaults. approach_axis is an Axis (unsigned). SurfaceTarget internals are deferred (inline object or reference).

target.description: SurfaceTarget — resolvable point + outward unit normal in a calibrated frame. Inline object or let-reference.

standoff.description: Length > 0 — terminal distance from the surface along the normal.

approach_axis.description: Axis — controlled-frame axis aligned anti-parallel to the normal (default embodiment.default_tool_axis).

clearance.description: Length >= 0 (default 0) — margin to the static model, excluding target.

contact_response.description: Reaction to contact before standoff (default abort).

ReachHoverParams.description: Parameters of reach.hover (01 § 1.5), precisely typed (approach B) — the twelve parameters of the § 1.5 table, no more. target + standoff are required; the rest carry the spec defaults. There is no timeout parameter (the hold is bounded by duration / the enclosing reactive). duration is Duration | until, not Duration | auto. target is a SurfaceTarget | FrameRef.

target.description: SurfaceTarget | FrameRef — reference to hover over; may be time-varying. Inline object or let-reference (a bare FrameRef name is also a reference).

standoff.description: Length > 0 — maintained distance from target along the normal.

approach_axis.description: Axis — axis held anti-parallel to the normal (default embodiment.default_tool_axis).

station_tolerance.description: Length — allowed positional excursion from the hover setpoint (default 2 mm).

duration.description: Duration | until (default until = defer termination to an enclosing reactive).

track_target.description: Follow a moving target vs. hold a fixed setpoint (default false).

settling_time.description: Duration | auto — max time to return within station_tolerance after a disturbance.

max_velocity.description: Velocity | auto — correction / tracking speed cap.

clearance.description: Length >= 0 (default 0) — margin to the static model, excluding target.

ReachScanParams.description: Parameters of reach.scan (01 § 1.6), precisely typed (approach B) — the thirteen parameters of the § 1.6 table, no more. region + standoff are required; the rest carry the spec defaults. The sweep pattern parameter is named pattern (enum raster / spiral / arc / waypoints, default raster) and the region parameter is named region. coverage_overlap is Ratio | auto. ScanRegion internals are deferred (inline object or reference).

region.description: ScanRegion — volume / surface / path to cover, in a calibrated frame. Inline object or let-reference.

sensor_frame.description: FrameRef — frame whose coverage matters (default embodiment.default_sensor_frame).

standoff.description: Length > 0 — sensor-to-region distance maintained during the sweep.

pattern.description: Deterministic sweep pattern over the region (default raster).

coverage_overlap.description: Ratio | auto — overlap between passes (default auto, derived from the sensor FOV).

sensor_axis.description: Axis — sensor axis pointed at the region (default the sensor descriptor bore_axis).

dwell.description: Duration (default 0) — hold time at each sweep pose for sensor integration.

max_velocity.description: Velocity | auto — sweep speed; also bounded by the sensor max_sweep_rate.

clearance.description: Length >= 0 (default 0) — margin to the static model over the sweep, excluding region.

Composition.description: A node of the compositional algebra (01 § Compositional algebra). Exactly one of: a primitive call, an extension call, or one of the combinators sequence / parallel / reactive / repeat / branch / let-bind. The forms are disjoint by key namespace, so a well-formed node matches exactly one.

PrimitiveCall.description: A core primitive invocation: a single key that is a PrimitiveId, mapping to its params (BNF Primitive ::= PrimitiveId "(" ParamList? ")"). Most primitives' params are an open object (#/$defs/Params); primitives precisely typed so far (approach B) additionally constrain their params via the conditional clauses in allOf. The open floor and the matching typed clause both apply to the same key, so the typed schema is what binds for those primitives; one if/then clause is added per primitive as the typing proceeds.

ExtensionCall.description: An extension primitive invocation (BNF Extension ::= "ext" "." Identifier "." Identifier ...). The id is ext.<namespace>.<name>; the registry (06-extension-registry.md) owns the namespace, not this schema.

Sequence.description: Ordered composition: each child runs to completion before the next (BNF Sequence). A let-bind child binds a name visible to the children that follow it in the same sequence.

Parallel.description: Concurrent composition of two or more branches (BNF Parallel).

Reactive.description: Run a body until a predicate confirms true (BNF Reactive ::= "reactive" "(" Composition "," "until" "(" Predicate ")" ")"). Per 01 § three-valued control flow the body terminates only on a confident true; a concurrent envelope violation takes precedence over a clean until completion.

Repeat.description: Repeat a body a fixed count or until satisfied (BNF Repeat ::= "repeat" "(" Composition "," Count ")", Count ::= Integer | "until_satisfied").

Branch.description: Three-valued conditional (BNF Branch). then / else are taken on a confident true / false; the optional unknown arm is taken on indeterminate, and without it an indeterminate predicate escalates rather than guessing (01 § three-valued control flow).

LetBind.description: Hoist a planner-derived value (typically a sense.* result) for reuse (BNF LetBind ::= "let" "(" Identifier ":=" Expression ")" "in" "(" Composition ")"). Concrete YAML form: a {let, from} statement whose binding scopes over the rest of the enclosing sequence; the BNF's explicit in(...) is accepted as the optional in key. Downstream uncertainty / measured-value flow checks are owned by 01 § LetBind flow checks, not this schema.

let.description: The bound identifier; later primitives reference its value by name.

from.description: The expression whose result is bound (typically a sense.* primitive call).

in.description: Optional explicit scope (BNF in(...)); omitted when the binding scopes over the rest of the enclosing sequence.

Predicate.description: A predicate of the algebra (BNF Predicate), consumed by reactive (until) and branch. A single key naming the predicate kind, mapping to its (here unconstrained) argument. value / confidence / evidence verdict semantics are owned by 01 § Predicates, verdicts, and three-valued control flow.
